items.message: The `claude` job fetches a GitHub OIDC token and writes it to `/tmp/gha-jwt`, but the job has no `if:` condition and no `needs:` on `gate`. It therefore runs unconditionally on every `issue_comment` event — including comments from untrusted actors — before the gate job can reject them. The token itself is short-lived and audience-scoped to `api.anthropic.com`, so the blast radius is limited to that federation trust, but the job also does `actions/checkout@v4` from an unvetted ref in this context…[truncated]

Same issue as in `implement.yml`: the `claude` job runs unconditionally on `pull_request` events with no `needs:` dependency. For `pull_request` from forks, `id-token: write` is typically suppressed by GitHub, so the risk is lower there, but on `push` or internal PRs the job mints and writes an OIDC token to `/tmp/gha-jwt` before any gating step can run.

The fetched OIDC token is written to `/tmp/gha-jwt` as a plain file with default permissions (world-readable on a Linux runner). Any subsequent step running in the same job — including a malicious action injected via a compromised dependency — can read it with `cat /tmp/gha-jwt`. Prefer writing to `$RUNNER_TEMP` with an explicit `chmod 600`, or passing the value through a masked environment variable rather than a file.

The `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` value is used without any validation of its scheme or host before being passed to `urllib.request.urlopen`. If an attacker can influence that environment variable (e.g. via a workflow that sets it), they can redirect the OIDC token request to an arbitrary URL, causing the runner to send its `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN` bearer credential to an attacker-controlled endpoint.
